pr_title: Implement slow-path PodTopologySpread logic without preFilterState
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind feature
/sig scheduling

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Implement the slow-path PodTopologySpread logic when preFilterState is absent. This is needed for CA (cluster autoscaler) so as to qualify this feature to be promoted to beta.

Unlike the preFilterState logic, when it comes to the slow-path, it means Filter() is called on every filteredNode and no calculation result is shared, so the logic is implemented differently, with a simplified data structure.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #87678

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

I assume in CA's perspective, only the filter plugin needs to implement the slow-path logic. Let me know if other case (preemption, score) is also needed.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
NONE
```

/cc @ahg-g @alculquicondor

> Thanks Wei, looks good to me.
> 
> I wonder if what CA actually needs is just a method to add/remove a node from prefilter state, and that can potentially be a lot faster for CA to simulate adding/removing nodes than computing the whole state all over again for each node.
> 
> /cc @MaciekPytel Łukasz Osipiuk
> adding CA folks for input

Thanks for work and looping us in!

With current implementation of CA based on scheduler framework (currently in review: https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/pull/2709), we are always calling all pre-filter plugins before filters. So I do not believe this code path will trigger at all. We are currently not doing any optimizations to limit amount of work spent in scheduler code. For each Pod, which we are simulating scheduling for, we are calling out both pre-filters and filters ([link](https://github.com/losipiuk/autoscaler/blob/lo/scheduler-framework-poc2/cluster-autoscaler/simulator/scheduler_based_predicates_checker.go#L224-L265)). Only optimization we have, is that if we want to check multiple nodes in a loop, we are calling to pre-filters once and then filters for each node ([link](https://github.com/losipiuk/autoscaler/blob/lo/scheduler-framework-poc2/cluster-autoscaler/simulator/scheduler_based_predicates_checker.go#L168-L214)).

We are not using methods which mutate `CycleState` at all right now. We might add those in the future. Yet they do not fit well in our code flow, and scale test so far showed that performance is good enough. Not worse that 1.16.

Do you guys expect that performance will get substantially worse with our approach, with equal-pods spreading enabled?

Only optimization we have, is that if we want to check multiple nodes in a loop, we are calling to pre-filters once and then filters for each node ([link](https://github.com/losipiuk/autoscaler/blob/lo/scheduler-framework-poc2/cluster-autoscaler/simulator/scheduler_based_predicates_checker.go#L168-L214)).

Thanks Lukasz!

I am not sure what your old approach, so I can't comment if it will get worse, but calling prefilters once and then filter on all nodes makes a lot of sense, that is what we do in the scheduler.

If your new approach is to call PreFilters always, then we would like to cleanup the similar logic in multiple other plugins (which is there only for CA). I will open an issue for that and cc you.

/hold

since we may not need this after all.

Only optimization we have, is that if we want to check multiple nodes in a loop, we are calling to pre-filters once and then filters for each node ([link](https://github.com/losipiuk/autoscaler/blob/lo/scheduler-framework-poc2/cluster-autoscaler/simulator/scheduler_based_predicates_checker.go#L168-L214)).

By old approach I meant the CA versions which were not based on scheduler framework. Then we called out to predicate functions directly and only computed predicate meta (which got replaced by pre-filters now) in subset of flows (almost never).

For scheduler framework based CA we always call out to pre-filters (as we kinda agreed on that before implementation :) ). 

And my question about regression was if performance will get worse when `PodTopologySpread` gets promoted to beta. I assumed that pre-filter related to that functionality is not present now, in the set of plugins registered by default. Am I right?

> If your new approach is to call PreFilters always, then we would like to cleanup the similar logic in multiple other plugins (which is there only for CA). I will open an issue for that and cc you.

Thx.

Thanks @losipiuk  for explaining the CA usecases in detail.

This PR is only useful if CA wants to call the Filter plugin individually. If you call multiple nodes in batch, then involving the preFilter is a better fit. 

> And my question about regression was if performance will get worse when PodTopologySpread gets promoted to beta. I assumed that pre-filter related to that functionality is not present now, in the set of plugins registered by default. Am I right?

Even with beta, which means PodTopologySpread PreFilter plugin is enabled by default, if the to-schedule pod doesn't need to be calculated (i.e., .spec.topolgoySpreadContraints is nil), then there is no performance overhead.
However, one thing _maybe_ worth noting is that, in the PreFilter function, the data structure of preState (we called it predicate metadata before) is designed for both Filter and Preemption - the part for Preemption may not be necessary for CA I suppose. In other words, if we don't consider Preemption, the memory print of the preState can technically be optimized a bit, for CA only, but the time complexity should be the same level.
I think in the past metadata calculation overhead wasn't zero for unused features, this has changed.
Closing this as we don't need keep the slow-path logic now.

issue_context.title: Calculate "preFilterState" for PodTopologySpread if it's not pre-calculated in preFilter plugin
issue_context.body:
Part of #87662.

In alpha phase, pod topology spread only works in defaultProvider, to promote it in beta, we should implement the slow-path preState calculation when it's not set:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cad44602e1188a1feff0bc085dc8286c6c5d3640/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/podtopologyspread/filtering.go#L296

/sig scheduling
/kind feature
/assign
comments: This is not valid anymore. See discussion in #87702.

review_comments:
To avoid more nesting, we could have:

```
testSingleConstraint(t *testing.T, runPreFilter bool)
TestSingleConstraint(t *testing.T) { testSingleConstraint(t, true) }
TestSingleConstraintNoPreFilter(t *testing.T) { testSingleConstraint(t, false) }
```
But up to you.

Calculating pre-filtered pod list doesn't look right as you can't only focus on matching Pods, instead, you need to also consider the case that nodes can be legit and don't have any matching Pod. In that case, the pre-filtered pod list lost that info.

I **_was_** thinking about calculating a pre-filtered node list, but it's only beneficial when len(constraints) >= 2, and given that it's a slow-path which we don't expect it to be executed by critical paths, so I gave up this idea.
got it, thx for detail explaination.
Should we add a `klog.V(5).Infof` here to be consistent with other returns?
What is the benefit of this versus calling `calPreFilterState`? At a quick glance, complexity looks the same.
